reports.text:
EXAM: CT chest without contrast.
INDICATION: Two-year surveillance after right upper lobectomy for stage IA adenocarcinoma.
COMPARISON: 07/22/2024.
FINDINGS: Stable postoperative right hemithorax. No new nodules or masses. No adenopathy. No effusion.
IMPRESSION: No evidence of recurrence.

documents.title: Oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Thoracic Oncology 01/22/2025: two years from resection without recurrence. Recent hospital stay for a bleeding ulcer noted; recovering. Moving to yearly CT, next January 2026. NKDA.

medications.drug: pantoprazole 40 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: PPI course
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with pt. Finished 8 weeks of pantoprazole BID this week. No pain, no black stools. Says he has not taken any naproxen since the hospital; acetaminophen for the knees is 'okay, not great'. Per GI discharge plan, stop pantoprazole now that he is off NSAIDs. Finish iron through early March. CBC 2/10. Bleed episode resolved on the problem list.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb back to 13.0. Good recovery. Finish the iron course. Pt notified.

documents.title: Iron pills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Took the last of the iron today. Do I need more? Happy to be done with them honestly.

documents.title: RE: Iron pills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No more needed - your blood count was back to normal in February. I've taken it off your list.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology visit
documents.author: transplant nephrology
documents.body: Transplant Nephrology, visit 03/19/2025 (moved up after his November GI bleed). Graft stable, creatinine 1.2, tacrolimus level in range through the admission. Strongly agree with permanent NSAID avoidance. Immunosuppression unchanged: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily. NKDA. Return in 12 months.

events.reason: Blood pressure and knee pain check-in

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from a hotel room on a run through upstate NY; connection fine.
Home BP log 120s-130/70s. No headaches.
Knees: acetaminophen takes the edge off; has cut long runs to 8 miles. Asked about naproxen once more - reminded him no NSAIDs, ever, after the bleed. He accepted that.
No GI symptoms since winter.
A/P: BP controlled. Knee OA on acetaminophen. Office visit in June for labs; physical in the fall.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: We missed you at your appointment yesterday. Please reply or call to reschedule.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry, got held at a dock in Maine an extra day. Just book me with the physical in the fall.

documents.title: Dermatology skin check
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body: Dermatology full-skin exam 07/31/2025. No recurrence at the right forearm Mohs site. Chronic photodamage only; no lesions requiring biopsy. Continue sun protection. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical. Turned 60 last month. Feels well. Still driving long-haul, talks about retiring in a few years. Running 2-3 days a week, shorter distances. No GI symptoms. Knees ache, acetaminophen helps. No dyspnea; hasn't used albuterol in months.

Problems: kidney transplant 2018 (graft stable), renovascular HTN s/p transplant renal artery stent 2022, stage IA2 RUL adenocarcinoma s/p lobectomy 1/2023 (NED, yearly CT), cutaneous SCC R forearm s/p Mohs 1/2024, duodenal ulcer bleed 11/2024 (resolved, NSAID-related), hyperlipidemia, COPD mild, bilateral knee OA, former smoker (quit 2021).
Meds: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg prn, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, fit-appearing. Skin: Mohs scar R forearm, sun damage L arm, nothing new. HEENT unremarkable. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, healed R thoracoscopy scars. Abd soft, nontender; transplant site nontender. Knees crepitus, no effusion. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
- Health maintenance: flu, updated COVID and RSV vaccines today (immunocompromised, age 60). Colonoscopy due 2027. PHQ-2 0.
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UA, urine albumin.
- Ulcer bleed: no NSAIDs. Reinforced.
- Transplant, oncology, derm follow-up per their schedules.
- Return in 6 months or sooner.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Charles - labs from Friday look good. Kidney function steady, blood count normal, cholesterol about the same, A1c normal, urine clean. Have a safe few months on the road and book your spring visit when you know your schedule.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department Physician Record
Arrival: 11/25/2025 21:10

CC: vomiting blood and black stools.
HPI: 60-year-old man, kidney transplant recipient, history of peptic ulcer disease with a bleeding duodenal ulcer last year, now with six hours of hematemesis and melena. Burning epigastric pain, worse over the past week. Reports he has gone back to over-the-counter naproxen for knee pain in recent weeks.
Meds: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, naproxen sodium 220 mg BID as needed (OTC).
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 95/60, HR 110. Pale, diaphoretic. Abdomen with mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Rectal: melena.
Labs: hemoglobin 9.2, hematocrit 27.8%, BUN 36, creatinine 0.9 (BUN/creatinine ratio 40).

ED course: IV access x2, fluids with improvement, IV pantoprazole, GI consulted. Admitted.
Impression: recurrent upper GI bleed, suspected recurrent NSAID-related peptic ulcer.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Discharge Summary
Admitted 11/25/2025, discharged 11/28/2025.
Diagnosis: upper GI hemorrhage from a duodenal bulb ulcer, recurrent, NSAID-associated.

EGD 11/26/2025: clean-based duodenal bulb ulcer without stigmata of recent hemorrhage; no endoscopic therapy needed. Stomach and esophagus normal.
Hemodynamics normalized with fluids. No transfusion. No further bleeding during the stay. Tacrolimus and prednisone continued.

Discharge medications:
NEW pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily
STOP naproxen - patient counseled again on strict NSAID avoidance
CONTINUE tacrolimus, prednisone, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP in 1-2 weeks with CBC.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital notified us of a second admission for a bleeding ulcer (11/25-11/28). Called pt: home, no further black stool, taking pantoprazole twice daily. Admits he went back to naproxen when his knees flared. Scheduled hospital follow-up with PCP 12/8 with CBC. Reviewed bleeding precautions.

documents.title: Hospital records received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record and discharge summary for admission 11/25-11/28/2025 received by fax and scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel today's hospital follow-up, back on the road - dispatcher needed him. Feels fine. Offered video visit; he'll call back with dates. Message to PCP.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for amlodipine 10 mg and HCTZ 25 mg, 90 days. Last visit 10/2025. Refilled x 1; pt still owes us a hospital follow-up, reminder sent.

documents.title: Oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Thoracic Oncology 01/28/2026: three years after resection, CT without recurrence. Had a second ulcer bleed in November, on pantoprazole since discharge. Next CT January 2027. NKDA.

documents.title: Dermatology skin check
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body: Dermatology full-skin exam 02/11/2026. Mohs site right forearm clear. No new suspicious lesions. Sun protection reinforced. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology annual visit
documents.author: transplant nephrology
documents.body: Transplant Nephrology, visit 03/11/2026. Eight years post-transplant. Graft stable, creatinine 1.2, tacrolimus level in range. Second NSAID-related ulcer bleed in November 2025 reviewed; he reports no NSAIDs since. Current medications per our list: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily since discharge. NKDA. Return 12 months.

documents.title: Refill and appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Need my atorvastatin refilled, down to a week. Also I know I owe you a visit, schedule is crazy until summer.

documents.title: RE: Refill and appointment
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Atorvastatin 40 mg sent to your pharmacy, 90 days. Please call the front desk when your summer schedule firms up - you are due for a visit and labs.

documents.title: Physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I get in for my physical sometime in October? Home most of that month.

documents.title: RE: Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Moran, the October schedule opens on September 1. We'll reach out then with a few morning options for your physical.
